A.text: Not even the healthiest person can. You only choose how you arrive.
A.changed: Moved 'Nobody skips a step of life' into the line. Text is now 'Not even the healthiest person can.', so 'skips' is not said twice. 'how READY you arrive' became 'how you arrive', since READY sits right above it.

A.text: Plato, the Greek thinker, wrote: "philosophy begins in wonder." Philosophy means the love of wisdom.
A.changed: Moved 'Life starts in WONDER' into the line. Quote, credit and the 'love of wisdom' line unchanged.

A.text: Thais say: "ไม้อ่อนดัดง่าย ไม้แก่ดัดยาก" (young wood bends easily, old wood is hard to bend). Old wood still bends, just slower.
A.changed: Moved 'Children learn to move through JOY' into the line (JOY teaches children to move). Saying, gloss and the 'still bends' line unchanged.

A.conn: of the strength you build yourself
A.text: A Swahili proverb: "Haba na haba hujaza kibaba" (little by little fills up the measure).
A.changed: Moved 'Strength you build yourself makes you PROUD' into the line. Saying and gloss unchanged.

A.conn: days come even to the strongest
A.text: Susan Sontag wrote: "Everyone who is born holds dual citizenship," one with the healthy, one with the sick.
A.changed: Moved 'Nobody is too strong to feel FRAGILE' into the line as 'FRAGILE days come even to the strongest' (word order fixed): the word names a time in every life, not the student. Quote and the healthy/sick line unchanged.

A.conn: grows each time you get back up
A.text: The Japanese say: "七転び八起き" (fall down seven times, get up eight). Your mat waits for you.
A.changed: Moved sentence 1 into the line word for word. Saying, gloss and 'Your mat waits for you' unchanged.

A.text: The Persian poet Ferdowsi wrote: "roam earth, converse with every one." Keep asking.
A.changed: Moved 'A CURIOUS mind stays strong without muscles' into the line (plural 'minds', so it reads as everyone). Quote and 'Keep asking' unchanged.

A.conn: like wise people who keep listening
A.text: A Korean proverb: "벼는 익을수록 고개를 숙인다" (the riper the rice plant, the more it bends its head).
A.changed: Moved 'Wise people stay HUMBLE and keep listening' into the line as 'HUMBLE like wise people who keep listening', which keeps the old meaning (v1 'is how' made humility the way they listen). Saying and gloss unchanged.

A.conn: later in life, that you kept moving
A.text: Russians say: "Береги платье снову, а здоровье смолоду" (care for clothes while new, health while young).
A.changed: Moved 'Later in life, you feel GRATEFUL you kept moving' into the line, with a comma so it reads in two parts. Saying and gloss unchanged.

A.conn: can still come, like a leaf going home
A.text: A Chinese saying: "落叶归根" (fallen leaves return to the roots). Thank your body.
A.credit: Chinese idiom · Jingde Record of the Lamp, c. 1004
A.changed: Moved 'A long life can still end in PEACE, like a leaf going home' into the line as 'PEACE can still come, like a leaf going home'. Keeps the hedge 'can still' from the wording put to Boonchu, so it is never a promise of a peaceful end. 'A long life' and 'at the end' cut to stay within 8 words; the leaf going home and the gloss carry the end gently. Saying, gloss, credit and 'Thank your body.' unchanged. Quote this exact line to Boonchu for his OK.

B.text: Not even a yoga master can skip one.
B.credit: The life of B.K.S. Iyengar · 9 steps · swipe
B.changed: Moved 'a WILLING heart climbs each one' into the line as 'hearts climb each hard step' (plural, so it is about everyone; it no longer ends like C1 'every step of life'). Text: 'Not even a yoga master can skip one.' No fact or quote.

B.text: B.K.S. Iyengar, who helped make yoga popular around the world, was born sick in 1918, then had malaria, typhoid and tuberculosis.
B.changed: The owner's own line. Moved 'began life HELPLESS' into it and joined the two sentences: 'He was born sick' became 'was born sick'. Every fact unchanged (Tribune, AP).

B.conn: about young Iyengar, even from his own teacher
B.text: He started yoga at 15, and his body was very stiff. Still, he would practise for hours.
B.changed: Moved 'Even his own teacher looked at him with DOUBT' into the line as 'DOUBT about young Iyengar, even from his own teacher': it now says who was doubted and by whom, so DOUBT cannot land on the man in the photo. 'young' is backed by Open ('the boy') and AP (age 15). Facts unchanged.

B.conn: is what the stiff boy became
B.text: He "could do a lot of backbends." At 18, when no one else would go to Pune, he went.
B.changed: Moved 'The stiff boy grew BRAVE' into the line ('grew' became 'became'). Quote and Pune line unchanged.

B.text: In 1979, his scooter hit a rock. "My spine was twisted." He was told he would never practise again.
B.changed: Moved sentence 1 into the line as 'HURT came to Iyengar too': 'the strongest body' read as a warning on the two students in headstand. 'too' keeps the idea that hurt comes to everyone, and 'his scooter' now clearly means Iyengar's. Facts and quote unchanged.

B.conn: is what healing took, even for a master
B.text: He said he recovered "only very slowly." He had to learn yoga all over again.
B.changed: Moved 'Healing took PATIENCE, even for a master' into the line as 'PATIENCE is what healing took, even for a master' (the approved claim: patience is what the slow recovery took; he healed by re-learning yoga, Tribune and Open). Quote and 'all over again' line unchanged.

B.conn: to keep writing, year after year
B.text: He mostly taught himself by watching how the body works. At 86 he published his 18th book.
B.changed: Moved 'An EAGER mind kept him writing into his 80s' into the line as 'EAGER to keep writing, year after year': '80s' could read as the age of the woman in the photo (Thai has no he/she) and said the age twice. The age now sits only in 'At 86'; 18 books by 86 backs 'year after year' (Tribune). Facts unchanged.

B.text: The wise old teacher said one woman practised for 11 years before she learned her knees were not straight.
B.changed: Moved 'The wise old teacher was CALM about slow progress' into the line as 'CALM because results take time' (Open: 'results took time'). Keeps the narrow point (calm about how long results take), with no claim about his general manner, and no 'his' or 'slow' to land on the man in the photo. 'He said' became 'The wise old teacher said'. Facts unchanged. CALM still waits for Boonchu's OK: quote him this line.

B.conn: to his practice in old age
B.text: In his 70s he could not climb stairs. Near 90, he did three hours of asanas daily.
B.changed: Moved 'In old age, he stayed LOYAL to his practice' into the line. Facts unchanged.

B.text: Even a strong body grows weak. He practised until two months before he passed away, aged 95.
B.changed: Moved 'The last step asks for a GENTLE heart' into the line as 'GENTLE hearts take the last step', which mirrors the B1 cover 'WILLING hearts climb each hard step' and drops one 'is' opener. Facts and the gentle 'passed away' wording unchanged.

C.text: You can learn it, even on the ones you wish you could skip.
C.changed: Moved 'stay STEADY on every step of life' into the line. 'You can learn to' became 'You can learn it', and 'the ones you wish you could skip' kept.

C.conn: by your own feet, as a baby
C.text: On the mat, you can look at your body like that again.
C.changed: Moved 'As a baby, you were AMAZED by your own feet' into the line. Second sentence unchanged.

C.conn: is how a kid can feel after falling
C.text: In a Mysore-style class, the teacher gives the next asana when you are ready.
C.changed: Moved 'As a kid, you could fall and still feel SAFE' into the line as 'SAFE is how a kid can feel after falling'. The kid comes before the fall, so it does not read as 'you are safe here even if you fall'. 'can feel' keeps it a feeling and a possibility, and 'a kid' (not 'you') does not assume the reader had a safe childhood. Mysore-style sentence unchanged.

C.conn: of yourself, from slow daily work
C.text: Same mat, same time. One day, you do an asana you could not do before.
C.changed: Moved 'Slow, daily work makes you SURE of yourself' into the line. Cut 'strong and': the new-asana line shows the strength. Rest unchanged.

C.conn: comes to us all when we get sick
C.text: Practice does not stop sickness. But you have a teacher who notices when you miss class.
C.changed: Moved 'Even healthy people get sick, and FEAR comes with it' into the line as 'FEAR comes to us all when we get sick': 'us' takes in the teacher and the viewer, so it does not point at the student in the photo. 'Practice does not stop sickness' and the teacher line unchanged. The photo move is still open (see rejected).

C.conn: starts the way back after sickness
C.text: You may return slower and weaker. But your mat and your practice time are still there, waiting for you.
C.changed: Moved 'Coming back after sickness starts with TRUST' into the line. Rest unchanged.

C.text: You learn your whole sequence by heart. Then you get a new asana and start again.
C.changed: Moved 'Your mind can stay OPEN to being a beginner' into the line ('Your mind can stay' cut). 'Then a new asana makes you a beginner again' became 'Then you get a new asana and start again', so 'beginner' is not said twice and 'one' cannot be translated as the number one.

C.conn: to yourself, after years on the mat
C.text: Some days the asana comes, some days not. You stop fighting yourself on hard days.
C.changed: Moved 'Years on the mat teach you to be KIND to yourself' into the line. Rest unchanged.

C.conn: is what strength means as you grow older
C.text: You get up from the floor on your own. Daily practice helps you keep more of that strength.
C.changed: Moved 'As you grow older, strength means feeling FREE' into the line. Rest unchanged ('helps... more of', never a sure result).

C.conn: can stay, even as the body weakens
C.text: Every practice ends the same way: rest, breathe, let go.
C.changed: Moved 'When the body gets weaker, the heart can still be at EASE' into the line as 'EASE can stay, even as the body weakens'. Keeps the hedge 'can' (never a sure result). 'weakens' kept so it does not echo B10 'grows weak'. 'in the heart' cut to stay within 8 words. Closing sentence unchanged.
